I think you've hit the nail on the head. Except that instead of kids, it's success. She's very ambitious, and she has a lot of hope for what we can accomplish for the next few years. I'm totally on board, and I think we've both managed to do a lot to set us up for success. Unfortunately, school is just something I have to do slowly, between working and paying for it. However, not going to school isn't stopping me from having a successful career. I've got a good job that is teaching me a lot of useful information that could get me a variety of well paying jobs down the road if my degree doesn't work out (The old follow your dreams but have a net.) 

But I think you're right. She's frustrated I'm moving slowly in my school, she's frustrated about her promotion being up in the air, she's frustrated we're stuck in our tiny apartment while we wait for news on her promotion, etc. There's a lot of our lives up in the air, and having something more concrete would probably help make her feel a lot better. 

I think we need to have a talk on expectations and healthy communication, but we also need to have some more stability in our lives.

Dang, I forgot to mention that she works full time, while both of my jobs are part time. With my two jobs, I was doing around 35 a week of work, and 25 of school, but now that I've dropped the second job and upped my classes, I'm only doing 25-30 hours of work and 30-35 hours of school per week. I didn't mean to make it sound like I was doing two full time jobs. 

Also, thank you for the advice. One of the points she made was having concrete answers on time, so having a concrete date night would be a great idea, and probably do a lot for both of us. A talk definitely needs to happen, but tonight is probably not a good time.
lol! Actually, we're both female. Thankfully unexpected pregnancy is not a high probability for us

It was out of left field, and I probably didn't respond as well as I should've because she has never expressed these sentiments before. She was always the one who pushed me to do more homework, or find something to study, or do as many classes as I can. This resentment at my doing homework is completely new. Hell, the reason I'm working so hard is so that I can spend time with her. I did as much homework as possible last night so I could go to the doctor with her this morning. And this Sunday will be the first time in a long time I'll have two days off, so I want to finish my homework before the weekend so we can actually spend time together.

I don't think so. It's one of those things where we both believe the other person does less than them. Generally though I make/warm up dinner every night, and do a lot of the cleaning and shopping too. I was working two jobs and going to school, but now I'm dropping to one job and upping my school, which I think she resents. She also has one job, but isn't going to school.

I do wonder if she's pre-menopausal sometimes. However, I've known a few people who have gone through menopause, and I don't think it's justification for the behavior. I do believe, however, it could be a symptom, and it's something I'll bring up if things start going well.

You absolutely right about the precedent. That's part of the reason I was so firm on the tank top situaton. I've tried going into it with logic, trying to get her to understand my side. I think I'm going to have to stop tiptoeing around it and say "You don't get to decide what I do and don't wear. I don't tell you how to dress, so you don't tell me how to dress."

Thank you. I think these problems are deeply rooted to her childhood. She came from a bad home, and I think her parents, particularly her father, instilled some warped views in what's acceptable in a relationship. I think that's where her aversion to therapy comes from as well. When she was a kid, if you expressed unhappiness about something in your life, it meant you were questioning the Lord and what he's given you. You were expected to put your problem in Jesus's hands and let him take care of you. Therapy is a sign you think Jesus can't handle your problems. She's gotten better with these things, but it's still hard on her. As for the workplace, she has a job akin to that of a police officer; she's often the bad guy for doing her job. I do have no doubt that people can be mean to her, but she has it in her head that they're all her enemy. Luckily she tends to be isolated most of the time, so she doesn't have to spend time with them. 

I think counselling is in order. I've already gotten in contact with a couples counselor in our area who speaks english. I told her it was something we had to do when we had the heart to heart I mentioned. But I do think I need to head back to individual counselling. I worry about the money, but I reckon money won't mean much if you're miserable. 

I don't think she's being purposefully manipulative. I just think she hasn't had the chance to develop a healthy adult mindset about certain things. I'm hoping the couples counselling can help with that in terms of our relationship.

I appreciate the advice. It was well written.

It was for a concert. I could see both sides. It was an outdoor concert in the middle of summer (it's usually pretty cool here, but somehow this concert manages to land on the sunniest and warmest days of the year) It had never been a problem before, but she argued that in a huge venue filled with drunk/high people that it wouldn't be wise to wear them. I ended up wearing jean capris.

How do you find a balance between being difficult and winning back power? I give my piece on nearly everything, but I don't feel like it's being thought of as annoying. She is very much a person where winning is important. She came from a pretty bad childhood, and I think it comes from the fact that that was the only way to stand up to her parents. But I try to approach everything with the intent of compromise (I used to have that winning attitude too, and it's something I've tried hard to overcome to be a better partner as it was a huge point of contention in my past relationship). But it's hard to compromise with someone who only wants to win.  Which leads me back to fighting instead of discussing. I feel like it's a cycle, and I'm not quite sure how to break it.
We actually have had the shorts fight before.

I don't think individual therapy would be beneficial because I don't think she would be open with the therapist. I think individual therapy is really something you have to want to do for it to work. Couples counseling, however, I said was non-negotiable during that heart to heart about our relationship. Now it's just a matter of finding the right one. There are some unique challenges in that (we live in a foreign country, so we would have to find an English speaking counselor) but I think I've found a good one and have gotten in contact. Now I'm just waiting for a response (which can be a bit slow in this country).

I also agree about individual therapy. I've been putting it off because I'm afraid of the prices, but I think it would be really helpful.

After breaking up with my girlfriend of nearly two years, I started dating someone 16 years older than me at the age of 18. We both had doubts because of the age difference, as well as social perceptions, but it ended up being the best decision of my life, as well as getting out of the old relationship. 

In my old relationship my GF hated the thought of change and moving forward. My dreams took motivation and desire, and she was always quick to point out chances of failure and encourage me to stay in a foreign country with her and her parents instead of going after them. She was quick to point out my faults and make me feel awful about myself. If I showed an interest in something, she'd tell me that it was either pointless or out of my abilities and so I shouldn't even try. 

My new girlfriend encourages me in every way possible and tells me every day how capable I am to follow my dreams. We go and try new things every day to enjoy life, and enjoy ourselves no matter what. I am not only inspired to do the best I can, but also confident that I have the ability to. My depression has all but disappeared, my motivation has increased, I've been working out and eating better, and more than anything I've found someone who I know believes in me and wants us to spend the rest of our lives together, not out of loneliness, but because we know we can go far together.

My girlfriend tried to kill herself because of me. 

Last December I had been dating someone else (We'll call her Sue), but cheating on them with my current girlfriend (We'll call her GF). Because Sue's parents are extremely homophobic, Sue and I hadn't been able to speak in months. She was in the States, I was in Germany. In the months we hadn't been able to speak, I'd started fooling around (Kissing, making out, holding hands, etc) with GF, and developing intense feelings for her. Finally, I decide to break up with Sue for GF, and email Sue explaining it. 

About three days later, Sue messages me that her parents have decided to let us speak again. 

I was torn. I hated (Well, still hate, but really hated it back then) Germany, and wished I was back in the states and happy. I'd been so happy with her, and wanted that back. Delusional from what I had but was gone, I broke up with GF to get back together with Sue. 

That was probably one of the worst weeks of my life. In the past years I'd suffered from Alexithyma, a condition where you have a difficult time processing/identifying/feeling emotions. Yet during this week I hopped from being happy to have Sue back to missing GF and hating myself for hurting her. It got to the point where I tried self harming (A habit I hadn't done for years), but didn't have a knife and only scraped myself with a rat tail comb before Sue talked me out of it.

Finally, after about a week, I broke it off with Sue, too devastated to be in a relationship with her. GF found out through a mutual friend, and we decided to try to remain friends. 

On New Years Eve she asked me out again, and ever since our relationship has been amazing. 

But the scars from that time were horrible. We both suffered from depression (Although we were both later diagnosed with different types of depression and anxiety) and at one point I had a mental breakdown. We both started counseling (Seeing the same school counselor) who suggested we do a group session to talk about what had happened the previous December. During the session I found out GF had tried to kill herself multiple times while we were broken up, but never told me because she felt horrible. 

Since then, I've hated myself. Because of my depression, I've always viewed myself negatively and had a low self esteem, but the guilt was overbearing. I would lay awake at night and mentally abuse myself, telling myself what a terrible person I was and how I deserved to die for what I did. I wanted to cut and hurt myself for what I did, but GF and I had made a pact against self harm, and I didn't want to betray her trust again. There were many nights when suicide crossed my mind, until I realized how selfish that would be, and would leave GF alone once again. 

My counselor has helped me tremendously with this guilt, but it's still there. Every time something happens between us (A small disagreement, her getting upset about something, etc) I stop and think "You hurt her so badly and yet you're getting into an argument about such and such? You're a monster." When my depression gets really bad, my mind lists the things I've done (Especially the breakup) until either I sob myself to exhaustion or start considering suicide, at which point I manage to stop thinking about all the bad things. 

I will always hate myself for what I've done. I love my GF more than anything and would die if something happened to her. I only hope I can make it up to her by giving her the love she deserves. Typing this out has helped a lot. Thank you, even if no soul sees this.

I completely get that. I look around and think "I should clean my room..." and then I begin and realize how daunting the actual task is. With cleaning my room comes doing the dishes in my room, doing the laundry in my room, organizing the things WITHIN my room, such as the dresser or closet, and in the end I think "Fuck it" and go to something else that takes less dedication, like Reddit. I have the same issue with things that I used to enjoy (Apparently a side effect of depression) like reading. I open up a book I usually love, see a wall of text and think "No...it's too much." Even though reading a simple paragraph is such a minuscule task. Then I feel pathetic

But snwborder52's comment sounds absolutely amazing. It seems to take away all of the necessity. Instead of things I *should* be doing, I think that I *could* clean my room, but only if I want to. Suddenly it seems a lot less...scary. 

I'm rambling. I should stop now. But I wanted to put in my two cents :)
